questions.question: A can complete one-sixth of a work in 5 days and B can complete one-fourth of the same work in 15 days. In how many days, will both working together complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

A can complete one-sixth of a work in 5 days and B can complete one-fourth of the same work in 15 days.

**Formula used:**

 If, A can complete a work in 't1' time and B can complete a work in 't2' time

then, A and B together can complete total work in ' t1 × t2 × 1/(t1 + t2) ' time

**Calculation:**

A can complete one-sixth of a work in 5 days

⇒ A can complete total work in 5 × 6 days = 30 days

B can complete one-fourth of the same work in 15 days

⇒ B can complete total work in 15 × 4 days = 60 days

∴ A and B together can complete total work in 30 × 60 × 1/(30 + 60) days = 30 × 60 × 1/90

= 20 days

questions.question: Sapna finishes a job in 12 hours working alone. If Sapna and Riya finish the same job in 8 hours working together at their respective constant rates, then, in how many hours can Riya do the job working alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sapna finishes a job in 12 hours working alone.

Sapna and Riya together finish the job in 8 hours.

**Formula used:**

Work rate of Sapna = dfrac{1}{12} job/hour

Work rate of Sapna and Riya together = dfrac{1}{8} job/hour

Let the work rate of Riya be dfrac{1}{x} job/hour

**Calculations:**

dfrac{1}{12} + dfrac{1}{x} = dfrac{1}{8}

⇒ dfrac{1}{x} = dfrac{1}{8} - dfrac{1}{12}

⇒ dfrac{1}{x} = dfrac{3 - 2}{24}

⇒ dfrac{1}{x} = dfrac{1}{24}

⇒ x = 24

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: P can fill a tank in 5 hours. Q can fill the same tank in 10 hours. R can empty the same tank in 20 hours. How much time will all the three take together to fill the same tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity (Total Work) = LCM(5, 10, 20) = 20 units.

Efficiency of P = 20 ÷ 5 = +4 units/hr

Efficiency of Q = 20 ÷ 10 = +2 units/hr

Efficiency of R = 20 ÷ 20 = −1 units/hr (negative work)

Combined efficiency = 4 + 2 − 1 = 5 units/hr

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time taken by pipe R to empty the tank = 20 hours

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Pipes & Cisterns vs Time & Work

The underlying concept is exactly identical to standard Time & Work. The only difference is that an outlet pipe or a leak is assigned negative efficiency.

Combined Efficiency Rule

If two pipes A and B can fill a tank in x and y hours, and pipe C empties it in z hours, their combined 1-hour work = (1/x) + (1/y) − (1/z).

Tank Capacity Formula

If the absolute flow rate (liters/min or liters/hour) of any pipe is known, then Tank Capacity = Total filling/emptying time of that pipe × Flow rate.

questions.question: P, Q and R can complete a piece of work in 9, 12 and 18 days, respectively. Working together, how much work can they complete in one day?

questions.question: If 27 people, working 8 hours a day, can complete a task in 12 days, then in how many days will 18 people finish the task, working 9 hours a day?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

27 people, working 8 hours a day, can complete a task in 12 days.

**Formula used:**

(M₁ × D₁ × H₁)/W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂)/W₂, where M, D, H, and W is the number of men, days, hours, and amount of work respectively. 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number of days required to complete the task by 18 people, working 9 hours per day is 'd'.

(M1 × D1 × H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W₂

⇒ (M1 × D1 × H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W2

⇒ (27 × 12 × 8)/1 = (18 × d × 9)/1

⇒ d = 16

**∴ The number of days required to complete the task by 18 people, working 9 hours per day is '16'.**

questions.question: A can do a certain work in 15 days, while B can do the same work in 21 days. If they work together, then in how many days will the same work be completed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two people **A** and **B**, combined time = (A × B) ÷ (A + B)

Time = (15 × 21) ÷ (15 + 21)

Time = 315 ÷ 36

Simplifying by 9: 315 ÷ 9 = 35 and 36 ÷ 9 = 4

Time = 35/4 = 8(3/4) days

**∴ The correct answer is 8(3/4) days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 15 days, Time taken by **B** = 21 days.

 
 

 **Person**

 **Efficiency**

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** of A and B = 7 + 5 = 12 units/day

⇒ **Total Time** taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 105 ÷ 12

⇒ Time = 35/4 = 8(3/4) days

**∴ The correct answer is 8(3/4) days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. If time ratio is x : y, then efficiency ratio is y : x.

One Day's Work

If a person completes work in 'n' days, then work done in 1 day = 1/n.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the **ratio of work done** or the **ratio of efficiencies** when people work for the same duration.</p

questions.question: Akhil can complete a piece of work in 24 days. Shyam can complete the same piece of work in 12 days. If both of them work together, in how many days can they complete the same piece of work?

Direct Formula for 2 Persons

Work and Wages

questions.question: 47 masons can dig a 35 m long trench in one day. How many masons should be employed for digging a 105 m long trench of the same type in one day?

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

The relationship between Men (M), Days (D), Hours (H), and Work (W) is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.

Direct Proportion

If two quantities are directly related (e.g., Work and Men), an increase in one results in a proportional increase in the other. In this case, M ∝ W.

Inverse Proportion

If two quantities are inversely related (e.g., Men and Days), an increase in one results in a proportional decrease in the other. In that case, M ∝ 1 ÷ D.
